channel.description: Latest articles from Global Competition Review (globalcompetitionreview.com)

item.title: We’ll do it live: The Tipline for 11 March 2026
item.description: What remains of the monopolisation suit against Live Nation will require some Louis Armstrong-type improvisation. Judge Arun Subramanian has summoned the “principal decisionmakers” in the case to appear for a hearing on Friday to determine whether to declare a mistrial or resume the case that was abruptly paused on Monday. Also in Tipline, Fanatics seeks sanctions for the “baseless” antitrust clai...

item.title: Leiweke’s counsel rebukes DOJ’s case
item.description: Counsel to Timothy Leiweke, the Oak View Group founder pardoned for big-rigging, said his client had strong legal arguments and economic analysis for having the case dismissed on the merits.

item.title: Take a swipe: The Briefing for 12 March 2026
item.description: Visa and Mastercard today attacked a landmark UK Competition Appeal Tribunal judgment that said all types of multilateral interchange fees were a breach of UK and EU antitrust rules. Exposed to further damages claims as a result, the companies today urged a UK appellate court to permit them to challenge the ruling, parts of which “lacked any sound evidential basis”. Also in The Briefing, advocate ...

item.title: PlayStation Store class action “fails at every step”, Sony says
item.description: Sony has attacked a £1.97 billion class action claim targeting its PlayStation business model, telling the UK’s Competition Appeal Tribunal that the antitrust lawsuit is based on a “selective and unreal approach” to its products and competition posed by rival gaming platforms.

item.title: Australian government bats back calls for ‘economy-wide’ divestment regime
item.description: Widening the Australian antitrust enforcer’s ability to seek divestment remedies to soften cost-of-living pressures and improve competition carries “more risks than benefits”, according to the country’s government.

item.title: Ribera: EU “better prepared” to tackle impact of energy crisis
item.description: The European Commission will draw on lessons from past crises as it remains watchful of rising energy prices stemming from the fallout of the war in Iran, according to EU competition chief Teresa Ribera.

item.title: Austria issues record €146 million penalty
item.description: Strabag has agreed to pay Austria’s highest-ever antitrust fine after being stripped of its leniency status in the country’s sprawling construction cartel probe.

item.title: AG Emiliou calls for General Court to rule again on JPMorgan and Crédit Agricole fines
item.description: Advocate general Nicholas Emiliou has provided a potential boost to JPMorgan Chase and Crédit Agricole’s appeals against a General Court ruling ordering the banks to pay fines of €337.2 million and €110 million.

item.title: My shot: The Tipline for 12 March 2026
item.description: Could Phil Weiser do for John Tunney what Lin-Manuel Miranda did for Alexander Hamilton? The Department of Justice has argued that the Colorado attorney general wants to turn the Tunney Act review of HPE/Juniper into “political theater” with live testimony from former Antitrust Division official Roger Alford. Also in Tipline, the DOJ warns against using competition law in trade disputes. &nbs...

item.title: Live Nation exec slammed concert goers as “so stupid”
item.description: A Live Nation executive bragged about being able to “take advantage of” concert goers with “fucking outrageous” prices, according to internal Slack messages unsealed by the US District Court for the Southern District of New York.
